status: draft — approved at the Stage 1B exit gate; Stage 2 normalizes IDs, structured fields, and enforcement mappings before this becomes canonical docs/testing/architecture-invariants.json entries

invariants.statement: A preview token is consumed exactly once, after validation and before the first await, so a replayed or concurrent confirm deterministically receives preview-stale.
invariants.linearizationPoint: The token delete precedes baseline resolution.
invariants.note: P5: comment and code currently disagree (groupCreationController.ts:686-689 vs :673-684); handled as an immediate standalone bug fix, not inside a migration slice.

invariants.statement: Manifest member state transitions have exactly one logical writer family routed through the lifecycle coordinator; finalize, failure settlement, and reconciliation demotion may not write around it.
invariants.authority: lifecycle coordinator (to be established in slice S2)

invariants.statement: A generation claim is durable before any terminal or provider side effect; claim removal requires proven-not-started evidence or an explicit user discard; ambiguity never auto-discards.
Dismissal persists the tombstone before removing any live row, context, or manifest member; a failed tombstone write refuses the whole dismissal.
The base ref is frozen to an immutable commit SHA before git worktree add; a group never provisions from a moving ref.

Every crash window between the seven linearization points has deterministic restart reconciliation: interrupted work demotes to failed/interrupted, tombstones prune only with positive evidence, unknown deletion observation keeps the lease.
invariants.authority: reconciliation controllers (manifest, provisioning, deletion journal, claims)

invariants.statement: Every pilot mutation message carries a correlation envelope (requestId, version) and a documented exactly-once mechanism (replay cache or single-use token); fire-and-forget mutation families are migrated or explicitly waived.
Domain identities (WorktreeKey, composite session identity, safe ids) use one canonical codec and equality policy owned by the domain layer; persisted encodings stay stable per usage context.
